subject: literature
passage: Every evening after the heat broke, Faisal climbed to the roof of his family's house in the old city of Lahore to let the pigeons out. The birds rose in a loose cloud, circled the minarets twice, and came back to him one by one. His favorite—a gray hen with a white collar and a crooked ______ always landed last, as if to make sure he had counted the others first. His mother said the pigeons were a waste of grain. Faisal did not argue, but he noticed that she, too, looked up when the flock passed over the courtyard.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: "A gray hen with a white collar and a crooked tail" is extra information describing "His favorite." It opens with a dash after "favorite," so it must close with a matching dash before the verb "always landed."
explanation.A: Incorrect. A semicolon would separate the subject "His favorite" from its verb "landed," and what comes before it is not an independent clause.
explanation.B: Correct. The second dash closes the pair around the description, so the subject "His favorite" connects to its verb "always landed."
explanation.C: Incorrect. Without a closing dash, the extra information is never set off and runs straight into the verb "landed."
explanation.D: Incorrect. Extra information that opens with a dash cannot close with a comma; the two marks must match.
